title: Data Interpretation: Tables and Charts: Quiz

questions.question: Sales in lakh rupees for 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 in order. Shop P: 40, 52, 60, 48; Shop Q: 55, 50, 65, 70; Shop R: 30, 36, 45, 54. By what percent did Shop P's sales rise from 2021 to 2022?
questions.rationale: Percent change = (52 - 40)/40 x 100 = 30%. Dividing by the new value (12/52 = 23%) is the common error; always divide by the old value.

questions.question: Sales in lakh rupees for 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 in order. Shop P: 40, 52, 60, 48; Shop Q: 55, 50, 65, 70; Shop R: 30, 36, 45, 54. What is the average annual sales of Shop Q over the four years?

Sales in lakh rupees for 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 in order. Shop P: 40, 52, 60, 48; Shop Q: 55, 50, 65, 70; Shop R: 30, 36, 45, 54. The ratio of the total four-year sales of Shop P to that of Shop Q is:
questions.rationale: P total = 200, Q total = 240. The ratio 200:240 simplifies by 40 to 5:6.

questions.question: Sales in lakh rupees for 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 in order. Shop P: 40, 52, 60, 48; Shop Q: 55, 50, 65, 70; Shop R: 30, 36, 45, 54. In which year were the combined sales of the three shops the highest?
questions.rationale: Yearly totals: 125, 138, 170, 172 for 2021 to 2024. The largest is 172 in 2024.

questions.question: Sales in lakh rupees for 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 in order. Shop P: 40, 52, 60, 48; Shop Q: 55, 50, 65, 70; Shop R: 30, 36, 45, 54. Shop R's 2023 sales are what percent of the combined 2023 sales of all three shops? (Nearest whole number.)

Sales in lakh rupees for 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 in order. Shop P: 40, 52, 60, 48; Shop Q: 55, 50, 65, 70; Shop R: 30, 36, 45, 54. Over which year did Shop R show the highest percentage growth compared with the previous year?
questions.rationale: R's growth: 20%, 25%, 20% for 2022, 2023, 2024. Absolute rises are 6, 9, 9, so 2023 and 2024 tie in absolute terms, but 2023 has the smaller base and hence the larger percentage.

questions.question: The pass percentage of a school rose from 60% to 72%. The percentage increase in the pass rate is:
questions.rationale: A rise of 12 percentage points on a base of 60 is 12/60 x 100 = 20%. The value 12 is the percentage-point difference, not the percent increase.

questions.question: In a pie chart of a family budget, Food takes 30%, Rent 25%, Education 15%, and the rest is Others and Savings. The central angle for Education is:
questions.rationale: A full circle is 360 degrees, so 15% corresponds to 0.15 x 360 = 54 degrees. 1% is 3.6 degrees.

questions.question: A monthly budget chart of total expenditure Rs 480,000 shows Rent as 25% and Food as 30%. How much more is spent on Food than on Rent?
The average monthly rainfall of five months is 50 mm. If four of the months had 42, 38, 55 and 47 mm, the rainfall in the fifth month was:
questions.rationale: Total needed = 5 x 50 = 250. Sum of known = 182. Missing = 250 - 182 = 68 mm.

questions.question: Marks out of 100 in Maths, Science and English: Asha 78, 84, 66; Bimal 90, 72, 63; Chitra 70, 88, 92. Who has the highest overall percentage?
questions.rationale: Totals out of 300: Asha 228, Bimal 225, Chitra 250. Chitra's 250/300 = 83.33% is highest.

questions.question: A factory's output fell from 60 thousand units to 48 thousand units. The percentage decrease is:
questions.rationale: Decrease = 12 on a base of 60 = 20%. A fall from 48 back to 60 would be a 25% rise, which is the reverse question.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best first step when you are given a data-interpretation table in an exam?
options: Read the title, units and column headings before calculating anything
Start calculating the largest value in every column
Assume all numbers are in the same unit
Approximate every value to the nearest ten and ignore the units
questions.rationale: Titles and units (lakh, thousand, percent, kg) decide the meaning of every number. Most DI mistakes come from ignoring them, so reading the labels first is the right habit.
